What a villa on Koh Samui costs

Prices are for the whole villa per night, not per person. The table shows typical low-season "from" rates in our listings; peak season usually adds 30–60 %, and Christmas to New Year has the highest rates and longer minimum stays (often 4–7 nights).

Villa sizeTypical guestsLow season per night (THB)Good for
2–3 bedrooms4–68,000–20,000Couples travelling together, small families
4–5 bedrooms8–1015,000–40,000Families, friend groups
6–10 bedrooms12–2030,000–120,000+Reunions, weddings, retreats

Good to know: many villas let you book fewer bedrooms at a lower rate; unused bedrooms stay locked and the villa stays private. Look for "3–5 bedrooms" in the villa details.

Best areas for a villa on Koh Samui

Chaweng Noi and Choeng Mon

Calm, swimmable bays on the north-east, 10–15 minutes from the airport and close to Chaweng's restaurants. The hillside villas above Chaweng Noi have the island's best sunrise views, but the access roads are steep. See Chaweng Noi and Choeng Mon.

Bophut, Fisherman's Village and Plai Laem

Restaurants, the Friday walking street and short drives to the airport and to Big Buddha pier for boat trips. The beach is shallow, so most villas here rely on their own pool. See Fisherman's Village and Bophut.

Maenam and Bang Por

Quiet north coast, long beaches with views to Koh Phangan, and the best value for larger villas. You will want a car. See Maenam.

Lamai and the south-east

Second-busiest beach town, good value, sunrise views, and quick access to Hin Ta & Hin Yai and the south-coast piers. See Lamai.

Taling Ngam, Lipa Noi and the west coast

Sunsets, calm shallow water and the quietest setting, 40–50 minutes from the airport. Pig Island and Koh Tan boats leave from Thong Krut nearby. See Taling Ngam and Lipa Noi.

Bang Kao and the south

Wellness resorts, sea views over Koh Madsum and Koh Tan, and short hops to Pig Island. See Bang Kao.

Tips before you book a villa

Book early for peak season

Christmas, New Year, Chinese New Year, Easter and July–August fill first. If your dates are fixed, book 3–6 months ahead; some villas give 5 % off for booking more than 180 days before the stay.

Check the road and the stairs

Hillside villas have the views but often steep concrete roads that scooters struggle with in rain, and many steps inside. Ask us about access if you travel with toddlers, older relatives or limited mobility.

Ask what is included

Check each villa's house rules: electricity is included in some villas and charged per unit in others; daily cleaning, pool service, Wi-Fi, a housekeeper, chef or breakfast vary. Each villa page lists inclusions and extra-cost services.

Deposit, balance and cancellation

Most villas need a deposit (often 50 %) to confirm and the balance 30–60 days before arrival. Cancellation terms are set by each villa and shown on its page; read them before you pay.

Transport and days out

A car or a driver makes villa life easier, especially on hillsides and on the west coast where Grab is thin. We arrange airport transfers, drivers, private chefs and our own boat trips to Ang Thong and Pig Island from your villa. See getting around Koh Samui.

Long stays

For stays of a month or more, many owners offer weekly and monthly discounts (often 10 % for 7 nights or longer). Visa rules changed in 2026: check our Thailand visa guide before planning a long stay.

How booking a villa works

  1. 1. Open a villa, pick check-in and check-out: you see a live price (or an estimate from the seasonal table).
  2. 2. Send a request with your details. No payment yet.
